text:
kai: FYI i'm bringing up a community model 'obelus-6b' for quant experiments and benchmark comparisons this week. license attached below, looks a bit ambiguous on redistribution/commercial benchmarking.

kai: License excerpt: "Model provided under Research-Only License v1.2 — no redistribution of weights; benchmarking allowed for non-commercial research; attribution required."

olivia: can you paste the exact clause that mentions redistribution? those words are key. also who upstreamed it? @sam?

sam: uploaded the tarball to /ml/models/obelus-6b.tar.gz. i ran a quick 4-bit quant with bitsandbytes: `python quantize.py --model obelus-6b --bits 4 --out obelus-6b-4bit.safetensors` — quality looked fine on synthetic conv evals but we haven't done human evals yet.

sam: curious if we are allowed to keep the quantized file in our internal artifact store and use it for hosted inference, or if that still counts as redistribution under the license.

olivia: reading v1.2, section 3: "Redistribution of model weights (including modified/quantized forms) is prohibited without express written consent." that suggests even internal artifacts might be risky if they can be exported to customers.

marta: saw a small regression on our chat-bench vs veridian-7b after quantizing to 4-bit — about -2.3% in helpfulness. before we dig legal, we should lock down evals and promptsets so we can show regressions.

legal-bot: Redirecting to licensing playbook: https://internal.redwood/legal/ml-licenses. Quick note: if the upstream license disallows redistribution of modified weights, you can still host the quantized model behind an API (inference-only) but cannot publish the quantized file or hand it to third parties.

olivia: summary: allowed: benchmarking (non-commercial research only per license), hosting behind our inference API for internal evals and demos, providing performance numbers in public as long as no weight redistribution. disallowed: distributing the quantized safetensors/.pt to external customers or OSS.

ian: for Dedicated customers: hosting in a Dedicated pool inside their VPC might be OK if we don't send them the file. but check contract — enterprise customers often require copy; that would violate the license.

sam: for our onboarding checklist, can we add a step: if license prohibits redistribution, do not check-in quantized artifacts to public S3 buckets or create exportable container images. mark artifact 'restricted' and set ACLs.

marta: also add a mandatory vendor clearance step before publishing any benchmark that could be used commercially; even if license says 'non-commercial allowed', marketing might treat it as commercial.

kai: good call. next steps: 1) sam to run the full eval suite and pin promptset (ETA tomorrow). 2) olivia/legal to confirm whether we can cite benchmark numbers in marketing (ask vendor). 3) ops to ensure artifact ACLs and flag in model registry.

ops-bot: created ticket ML-4823: "Obelus-6b license clearance + restricted artifact handling" and set priority P2.

olivia: i'll reach out to upstream with a short request template: "request to clarify whether quantized derivative distribution and commercial benchmarking are permitted; if not, do you offer a commercial license?" will paste draft here.

sam: thanks. i'll hold off publishing any artifacts or sharing safetensors until we get a greenlight. :thumbsup:

marta: i'll freeze the eval comparisons and save the current run outputs to the restricted folder.

kai: thanks everyone. tagging @legal-bot if we need standard NDA/clarity template.
